findings.issue: As the orchestrator decided, errClientUnavailable is the lowercase sentinel "workiva client is not available", which replaces the plan's capitalised wording. Because it is unexported, the prepare_section tool in package tools (T5) cannot use errors.Is on it to turn it into a capitalised failMsg. The tool will show the lowercase text as it is. That is acceptable under the decision. It is recorded so T5 does not expect an exported sentinel.
findings.fix: None required for T4. If T5 needs to match the error, export the sentinel (ErrClientUnavailable) in that task's scope.

findings.issue: The a1 blocking ST1005 finding is fixed. errClientUnavailable is now a plain lowercase errors.New sentinel that Prepare returns directly (line 103). There is no providerName indirection, no nolint or lint:ignore comment, and golangci-lint reports 0 issues. The sentinel is unexported, though, so the T5 tool layer cannot use errors.Is on it to produce the capitalised failMsg("Workiva client is not available", ...) that the other tools return (get_field.go:97, read_range.go:62). Through fail(err, ...) the agent will see the lowercase text.
findings.fix: This is optional. If T5 or a later task wants the tool-layer wording to match the other tools, export the sentinel (ErrClientUnavailable) and map it there. Otherwise leave it as the orchestrator decided.

findings.issue: This was carried over from a1. The min/max check still loops over an anonymous struct slice that holds comparison closures. For two fixed bounds this is harder to read than two plain checks. Some names are still vague: `in`, `more`, `b`.
findings.fix: Write two explicit checks through a small helper, and name the variables more clearly, for example factIn and rangeFindings.

findings.issue: This was carried over from a1. The sign_change check compares canonical decimal strings to "0" and uses a prefix check for sign. That is only correct because Fact.Current and Fact.Prior are always canonical, and this call site does not say so.
findings.fix: Use assurance.CompareDecimal against "0", or add a one-line comment that cites the canonical-form guarantee.
